evidence: De La Soul's 1989 debut established the sample-collage, wordplay-heavy style and public identity later named the 'Native Tongues', which A Tribe Called Quest, whose own debut came a year later, is consistently described as sharing and extending. Q-Tip appears alongside De La Soul, Jungle Brothers, Queen Latifah and Monie Love on the 1989 'Buddy' remix, credited on the single's own release, months before A Tribe Called Quest's first album. Critics and historians name the two groups together as founding members of the same loosely affiliated collective, without a single first-person statement from either side calling it direct influence.

later.title: People's Instinctive Travels and the Paths of Rhythm

explanation.age7: De La Soul and A Tribe Called Quest were friends who made music the same relaxed, playful way. De La Soul's first album came out a year before Tribe's.
explanation.age13: De La Soul's 1989 album came out a year before A Tribe Called Quest's first record, and both were part of a loose group of rap acts called the Native Tongues, who shared a warm, sample-heavy sound and a friendly attitude. Q-Tip from Tribe even rapped on a De La Soul remix, 'Buddy', before his own group's album came out.
explanation.adult: The Native Tongues were never a label or a formal group, just a shared identity among acts (De La Soul, A Tribe Called Quest, Jungle Brothers, Queen Latifah, Monie Love and later others) who supported each other's records and shared a sound. De La Soul got there first, and this edge is best read as a collective identity forming around a style De La Soul introduced, not a specific, named act of transmission, which is why it sits at consensus.
